title: Novus Skyline LLM gateway — integration scratch jottings
content:
Meeting: Novus Skyline kickoff (on-site sync) — 2025-11-19
Attendees: Evan (RWI SE), Priya (RWI infra), Liam (RWI SRE), Julia Park (Novus infra lead), Marco Ruiz (Novus ML eng), Denise K. (Novus security)

High-level ask
- Replace current in-house light-weight LLM gateway with Redwood-hosted/private combo.
- Goals: consistent 99th pct latency <300ms for short queries (<=256 tokens), cheaper per-token for bulk semantic search (embeddings), deterministic fallback when dedicated capacity exhausted.
- Must support VPC Private deployment (Novus requirement) with customer-managed KMS and audit logs.

Quick client context / constraints / nuance
- Novus runs critical inventory and pricing features; even small latency regressions impact conversion.
- Sensitive PII in prompts (customer names/locations). They require encryption at rest and in transit, plus key material in their KMS (no managed keys).
- Current workload: 12M requests/mo, 70% embeddings (short), 30% chat/generation (mostly <200 tokens). Peak QPS roughly 150 sustained with spikes to 400 (seasonal).
- They use multi-region (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 DR). Prefer local processing for EU traffic.

Architecture notes from call
- Novus wants Private (VPC) control plane + on-prem inference nodes for the most sensitive tenants (hybrid).
- Networking: requirement for VPC peering + strict egress policy (no public IPs from inference instances).
- DNS: they will own certs and internal DNS mapping. Need docs for private endpoint bootstrap.
- KMS/HSM: they will provide key material. We need to validate Redwood Private supports BYOK flow they want (HSM-backed key rotation cadence).

Performance / runtime considerations
- Sequence lengths for generation: typically 64–180 tokens. Rare long-running jobs (>=1024) for analytics — plan separate routing.
- Embedding batch size: they push batches of 512 rows via bulk endpoint. Recommend batching guidance: embedding batching with dynamic batching window (80–120ms) and per-tenant batching caps.
- KV cache: heavy reuse for chat flows (prefix reuse). Ensure we enable prefix/KV caching on dedicated pools for those tenants to hit latency SLO.
- Quantization: Novus tests show minor output drift on int8 for BLIP models. They want to avoid aggressive quantization on chat model variants. Recommend minimal (nf4) quant profiles and validate locally.

Gotchas / red flags mentioned
- Network egress policy may block Redwood autoscaling agents. Need offline install docs or relay system.
- Compliance: they need detailed audit logs with per-request PII markers redacted but traceable. Confirm Redwood’s audit retention and redaction knobs.
- Rate shaping: Novus has internal burst patterns (500 qps for 30s every 3 hours). Autoscaling / warm pool must cover those bursts; discuss warm standby vs instant scale.
- Embedding consistency: their semantic search pipeline expects deterministic embeddings for the same inputs; confirm floating-point/quantization determinism across rollouts.

Decisions / verbal agreements in call
- Proof-of-concept: initial POC will run in their VPC with 2 dedicated GPU nodes for 4 weeks. Use model variant rwi-embed-large-v1 for embeddings and rwi-chat-small-v2 for gen.
- SLOs: target median latency <120ms for embeddings, p99 <350ms for chat on dedicated nodes.
- Security: Novus will provision KMS keys and provide access; Redwood to provide BYOK integration checklist and a short-run key rotation test.

Immediate next steps (owner / due)
1) Send VPC bootstrap doc + checklist to Julia (Novus) — Evan — due 2025-11-22. (Checklist: VPC subnet layout, NACLs, route table examples, bootstrap IAM role, egress relay config)
2) Draft BYOK/HSM integration flow + sample KMS policy — Priya — due 2025-11-25.
3) Create infra PR for warm-pool warmup policy templates (config options for dedicated) — Liam — due 2025-11-28.
4) Provision POC environment and schedule kick-off run (2 GPUs) — Evan/Priya — target start 2025-12-01.
5) Create evaluation prompt set and embedding validation harness (determinism tests) — Marco/SE — due 2025-12-03.
6) Ask legal for DPA checklist and retention limits required — Evan — due 2025-11-24.

Notes to self (informal)
- Ask SRE about agentless scaling/relay options — can't assume outbound to internet. Possibly use SSH relay or AWS PrivateLink to Redwood control plane.
- Prepare a small non-prod demo showing prefix caching impact on p99 for chat (50% improvement observed on similar workload).
- Quantization: schedule microbenchmark with Priya for rwi-chat-small-v2 at nf4 vs int8 to quantify hallucination/regression risk.

Open questions for Novus (send as email after POC doc)
- Can they accept a small egress to Redwood control plane for lifecycle events (TLS only)? If not, we need completely offline install path.
- How many distinct tenant namespaces will be in single VPC? Multi-tenant inside their VPC complicates per-tenant billing / quotas.
- Embedding determinism acceptance criteria: what similarity delta is acceptable post-rollout? (e.g., cosine diff < 1e-6?)
- Do they require on-prem inference nodes to be fully air-gapped for specific customers? If yes, need different provisioning path.

Suggested tickets to open (internal)
- SE-5807: Novus POC bootstrap doc (Evan)
- INFRA-3221: Warm-pool templates + autoscale relay (Liam)
- SECURITY-1472: BYOK test flow + audit retention mapping (Priya)
- EVAL-210: Embedding determinism harness for Novus (Marco)

Commercial notes
- Novus asks for discounted committed capacity if they move majority of workload to Dedicated within 90 days post-POC. Flag to AE for heads-up.
- They asked about trial credits for first month — offer 50% credits on Dedicated reserved trial (discuss with Sales).

Follow-ups done / status
- Bootstrapped initial Confluence page and uploaded this scratch doc — Evan — 2025-11-20.
- Slack thread created for Novus infra questions (link above).

Longer-term ideas (brainstorm)
- Offer embedding determinism SLA for paying customers (runs on dedicated pools with locked kernel versions).
- Provide an offline-only control plane release (air-gapped) for clients with extreme regulatory needs (packaged install + local dashboard).

Comments / random thoughts
- Keep POC narrow: verify network + KMS + latency. Avoid rolling model variants until network/ops story is solid.
- If egress-blocked, propose a small AWS PrivateLink endpoint as the simplest path.

---
End of notes. Save as canonical scratch until POC kickoff.
